items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Billie wanted us to record with her so we recorded after we got off that night... I recorded with Billie Holiday there

ctx.x: Did you play with him then (inaudible).

At the after hours, no, I -- then I'd listen, I'd just sit here and listen. As a matter of fact the first time -- he introduced me to Billie Holiday. She came to Chicago to work the Grand Terrace, and we met her, our first night there we met her in the after hours spot and we hung out that morning until about -- that day until about 12:00 o'clock the next day just playing and just having a ball, you know.
But any way, I -- after Art left, Roy left Fletchers.

items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: John Hammond at this time was interested, still interested in Prez. But as I told you before, in the back of his mind he had -- wanted Prez to be the backup for Billie Holliday. And when Prez found this out he refused.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. Yeah, well that's evident by size, you know. But Harold was a marvelous cook, and so we would just pool our money and give Harold -- we would buy the groceries and Harold would cook, you know. And this -- I think this is why -- this is how we started rehearsing together, Lester, Harold, and Shad Collins used to come around all the time. And when they -- Shad had played with Basie also, and we got a bass player by the name of Nick Fenton, as I told you, and this is how we started rehearsing. We just…
before, in the back of his mind he had -- he wanted Prez to be the backup for Billie Holliday. And when Prez found this out he refused.

But Prez was a very -- he was a very earthy man. He had earthy sayings, very profound sayings, very profound man. You know, he could say things that would really hit home, but they were really home sayings. You know, they weren't very -- what can I say intellectual or something, but really, really hit --
